public_rationale: All three parts hold on the plain reading for early 2024. Hallucinations: a January 2024 Stanford study found hallucination rates of 69% to 88% on specific legal queries for leading models, including OpenAI's GPT-3.5. Energy: the IEA projected in January 2024 that data-centre electricity demand, driven partly by AI, could double by 2026. OpenAI's CEO said that month that AI would need an energy breakthrough. Compute costs: the WSJ reported that Microsoft lost more than $20 per user per month on its $10 GitHub Copilot in early 2023. None of this suggests a solution was close. The IEA did expect clean energy supply to cover new demand, which softens the energy point but does not solve AI's power needs.
limitations: 'Not close to being solved' has no stated measure. The verdict uses an ordinary reading.
The profitability evidence is a single anonymously sourced report about one product.
The hallucination study covers legal queries and GPT-3.5, not every model or domain.

statement.excerpt: Generative AI's core problems — its hallucinations, its massive energy and unprofitable compute demands — are not close to being solved.

from_speaker: are not close to being solved
our_interpretation: Plain reading: in early 2024, each of the three problems was still large and unresolved, with no solution near deployment. (1) Leading models still hallucinated at meaningful rates. (2) AI's electricity demand was large and expected to grow, not shrinking. (3) Serving generative AI often cost more than it earned.
Target period: from the start of 2023 to the post date. This is the latest evidence available before the post on a present-tense claim. Chosen by the evaluator.
criteria.support_condition: In-period evidence shows each of the three problems was still serious and that no near-term fix was in view.
criteria.contradiction_condition: In-period evidence shows that one or more of the problems was solved or close to it. Examples: hallucinations near zero, AI energy demand flat or falling, or generative AI services broadly profitable to run.
